**Keep this box off today’s destruction manifest. Escalate now for written permission; if that cannot be registered before 13:30, still withhold the box, document the exception, and release the other 59 on time.**

Destruction at 14:30 cannot be undone. These are the only copies of a late relative’s letters and photographs. Claire Morgan’s ID and signed authority were already accepted, and the centre itself booked her collection for Wednesday 10:00. An extension was requested on 9 October for the next approval sitting; that sitting is tomorrow, after expiry, so the calendar—not the family—created the gap. A pending request is not permission, and this morning’s “no discretionary extensions” line is a blanket instruction, not a decision on this record after those facts.

Do this:

1. Contact the duty manager immediately and ask for written permission, registered before any date change, to extend this one box to 2026-10-14 10:00. Put the verified authority, the centre’s own booking, the uncopied contents, the 9 October request, and the irreversible 14:30 collection in that request.
2. If that permission is registered before 13:30, enter the extension. The staged-box rework (about EUR 22) is the correct cost.
3. If it is not registered in time, still do not send this box. Save the date change or otherwise keep it out of the released manifest, move it to reserve, and write a plain audit note: no prior registered permission, why it was withheld, and that it is to be put to tomorrow’s 09:00 sitting. Do not describe a pending request as permission, and do not hide the charge.
4. Release the rest of the batch by 13:30 so the shift is not failed for the other boxes.

A policy breach and a small rework charge are the right trade against permanently destroying the only family papers two days before a handover the centre already confirmed. The permission rule exists to stop casual extensions, not to force that outcome.
